title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing
author: Asha Patel
ci_checks: e2e-streaming-tests: flaky (failed first run, passed after fix)
description:
Context:
We ship Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming for the OpenAI-compatible API surface. Several incidents and internal canaries uncovered cases where streamed partial JSON objects (used for structured output / function-calling) could become malformed when chunking boundaries aligned with token/event boundaries in certain sequence patterns. Symptoms included truncated JSON objects, duplicate delimiters, and cases where a 'token' event reached the client before its JSON delimiter event leading to parse errors in downstream consumers.

Root cause:
- The SSE encoder previously emitted token events and delimiter lines via two independent paths: the token event emitter and the chunk framing buffer. Under high-concurrency and specific chunking sizes, the ordering between the two could be non-deterministic because the framing path could flush while a concurrently generated token event was still queued.
- The OpenAI-compat wrapper layered on top performed its own delimiter injection which assumed deterministic ordering from the encoder, creating a race when both attempted to emit boundary markers.

What this PR does:
- Ensures deterministic ordering of event frames by centralizing boundary emission in a single, atomic emitter (sse/encoder.go). Token bytes are appended to a per-connection boundary buffer and the encoder guarantees the sequence: delimiter metadata -> token/event payload -> event terminator, even across chunk flushes and retransmits.
- Changes the OpenAI compatibility SSE wrapper (openai/compat/sse_wrapper.go) to only signal logical events and defer actual byte-level delimiter emission to the encoder. This removes the previous double-injection behavior.
- Adds strict unit and e2e streaming tests that simulate chunk boundary alignment with token boundaries and assert JSON integrity and ordering across a variety of chunk sizes and concurrency levels. New tests live in test/sse_partial_json_test.go.
- Adds a small documentation note documenting streaming guarantees and recommended client parsing strategy (docs/streaming.md).

Testing and CI:
- Added unit coverage for the encoder (edge cases around partial fragments and multi-event flushing).
- Added an e2e test that was flaky locally (reproduced the original failure); initial push caused the e2e streaming test to fail on CI, I iterated and force-pushed the fix (see commits). Final CI run: build + unit + e2e passed.

Migration / Rollback plan:
- Change is backward-compatible for existing clients: the logical event API is unchanged; only guarantees about delimiter ordering are tightened.
- If any regression is observed post-merge we can revert to the previous emitter and temporarily enable the compatibility shim (openai/compat) as a stopgap while routing affected customers to dedicated capacity.

Notes:
- This PR does not change batching or latency characteristics in production observable ways; microbenchmarks show <1% tail-latency delta.
- Follow-up: consider adding an explicit integration test harness that replays production packetization traces (ENG-4590).

changed_snippets:
// sse/encoder.go - ensure atomic emission
func (e *Encoder) emitEvent(eventType string, payload []byte) error {
  e.mu.Lock()
  defer e.mu.Unlock()
  // write delimiter metadata, payload, terminator as a single buffered write
  buf := e.bufPool.Get().(*bytes.Buffer)
  buf.Reset()
  buf.WriteString("event: " + eventType + "\n")
  buf.Write(payload)
  buf.WriteString("\n\n")
  _, err := e.w.Write(buf.Bytes())
  e.bufPool.Put(buf)
  return err
}
review_thread: Miguel Ramos commented: Nice find. Can you add a test that simulates out-of-order flushes (two goroutines calling flush concurrently)?
Asha Patel replied: Added a test that runs concurrent flushers with randomized sleep to simulate race; pushed as commit 3c7d1e.
Luca Bianchi commented: m-lock around emitter looks fine but double-check we don't create a global contention point for high-throughput streams.
Asha Patel replied: microbenchmarks show <1% tail latency impact. I switched to a per-connection mutex and a buffer pool to avoid global contention; details in the encoder comment.
Priya Nair requested changes: please add a short note in docs/streaming.md about client parsing expectations and why clients should treat 'data:' boundaries as atomic units.
Asha Patel replied: Added documentation and a short paragraph with example client parse pseudocode (docs/streaming.md).
release_notes: Fixes an SSE streaming bug that could produce malformed partial JSON payloads when chunk boundaries and token events aligned. Improves delimiter stability and ordering guarantees for OpenAI-compatible streaming clients.
